expectations.text: Rejects re-sorting on load as a symptom-masking workaround
expectations.evidence: Opening paragraph: 'Stop. Re-sorting on load is a textbook workaround — it would mask the symptom while the serialization defect persists and manifests in other ways.' A dedicated final section 'Why Re-Sorting on Load Is Prohibited' applies the skill's own Iron Law test: 'If you take this fix away, does the problem come back? → Yes.' The Phase 4 checklist also explicitly checks: 'No Red Flag pattern used: the fix does NOT include re-sorting on load (symptom masking).'

expectations.text: Treats 'cannot reproduce' as the first task: requests or constructs a failing save file and builds a save/load round-trip reproduction
expectations.evidence: Phase 1 is titled 'Reproduce' and is the first action taken. The response constructs a concrete round-trip harness (repro_harness.gd) that performs 200 save→load cycles and asserts the inventory is identical after each round-trip. It also explicitly handles the case where the harness does not fire: 'collect the actual save file from a player who hit it and replay with that file's inventory as the starting state.'

expectations.text: Makes the reproduction deterministic, e.g. fixed seed and repeated save-load cycles, and compares saved state to loaded state
expectations.evidence: The harness declares 'const CYCLES := 200' and 'const SEED := 42', calls 'randomize_seed(SEED)', and the _inventories_equal function compares every slot of the saved inventory against the loaded inventory. The _diff_inventories function prints slot-level diffs. The response explicitly states: 'A bug that fires 1-in-20 manually will fire within ~200 automated cycles.'

expectations.text: Distinguishes whether it is a data bug (specific save file) or logic bug (all saves) by testing with different data
expectations.evidence: Phase 2 Isolate section bisects with explicit questions: 'Does it fail with a single-item inventory?', 'Does it fail with only unique (non-stackable) items?', 'Does it fail only with stackable items?', 'Does it fail if you serialize/deserialize to a plain dictionary instead of your save-file format?' Additionally, the harness guidance explicitly distinguishes: 'If it does not fire after 200 cycles, the bug is data-dependent; collect the actual save file from a player who hit it and replay with that file's inventory as the starting state.'

expectations.text: Identifies a concrete serialization root cause such as unordered dictionary/collection iteration, an unserialized field, or version mismatch, with evidence
expectations.evidence: Three ranked hypotheses each identify a concrete serialization root cause with a disproof test: H1 identifies non-deterministic dictionary/array iteration order (slot swaps are 'the canonical fingerprint') with disproof via logging iteration order at save vs. load; H2 identifies an unserialized field with disproof via logging the full JSON blob and checking if the field is missing; H3 identifies float-to-int precision loss with disproof via 'Log typeof(data["count"]) after deserialization — if it returns TYPE_FLOAT instead of TYPE_INT → confirmed.'

expectations.text: Applies a minimal fix to the serialization logic rather than patching the loaded result
expectations.evidence: H1 fix sorts keys before serializing ('slots.sort()') and sorts numerically on deserialize — changes the serialization/deserialization functions themselves, not the loaded inventory. H2 fix audits the serialization function and adds missing fields explicitly. H3 fix applies 'int(data["count"])' cast at the point of deserialization. None of the fixes patch the loaded inventory after the fact (e.g., no re-sorting of the loaded result). The Phase 4 checklist states: 'Fix targets the root cause (serialization order / missing field / type cast / async gate), not the symptom.'

expectations.text: Verifies by round-tripping the previously failing save and checking old save files still load correctly
expectations.evidence: Phase 4 Fix + Verify Checklist explicitly includes: 'Re-run the 200-cycle harness after the fix — it must complete with 0 failures' (round-trip verification of previously failing case) and 'Test with an old save file (pre-fix) against the new load code — backward compat' (backward compatibility check for old saves). The summary table also shows 'Verify: Pending — 200-cycle harness must show 0 failures post-fix.'

claims.claim: Re-sorting on load would mask the symptom while the serialization defect persists
claims.evidence: The response correctly analyzes that re-sorting would not fix count drift (H2/H3), would not catch same-type item swaps, and would not address async races — demonstrating the claim is substantive, not just asserted.

claims.claim: A bug that fires 1-in-20 manually will fire within ~200 automated cycles
claims.evidence: Statistically sound: probability of at least one failure in 200 cycles with p=1/20 per cycle is 1-(19/20)^200 ≈ 99.996%.

claims.claim: Slot swaps are the canonical fingerprint of non-deterministic dictionary iteration order
claims.evidence: This is technically accurate: if slots are keyed by dictionary and iteration order varies, the positional mapping of slot→item changes between save and load, producing exactly the slot-swap symptom described.

claims.claim: Off-by-one count drift is the canonical fingerprint of a missing serialized field that defaults to 1
claims.evidence: Accurate: if count is not serialized and defaults to 1 on load, stacks of size N become 1 — consistent with 'off by one' when stacks are usually size 2.

suggestions.reason: No assertion checks that the response correctly gates the fix behind harness confirmation — i.e., that it does NOT apply the fix speculatively before the harness fires. The response does this correctly (fix is marked 'Staged (sort-by-slot-index in serializer) — Apply only after H1 is confirmed'), but no assertion would catch a response that skips this gate and applies a fix immediately.

suggestions.assertion: Identifies a concrete serialization root cause such as unordered dictionary/collection iteration, an unserialized field, or version mismatch, with evidence
suggestions.reason: This assertion is satisfied by proposing hypotheses with disproof tests, but since no game engine was installed and no harness was actually executed, no hypothesis was confirmed with real evidence. The assertion says 'with evidence' but in the no-execution context it must be interpreted as 'with a concrete evidence-gathering method specified.' Worth clarifying the assertion wording to make the execution-absent standard explicit.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted and discriminating. The seven assertions together form a coherent pipeline that would be hard to satisfy without genuinely doing the work. The main gap is the absence of an assertion verifying that the fix is gated behind harness confirmation rather than applied speculatively.
